qa.asked:
I've picked the case: this is a **New** build, a Read-and-lookup page in plain HTML, CSS and JS. The design process asks me to settle a few things before I build, so I need your answers to four questions. The first option in each is what I'd recommend.

**1. How should members look things up?**
- **a) Search plus filters (recommended).** Members type a name, or narrow by habitat, season, and cap or gill type. This works for people who don't know the name yet, which is most foray finds.
- b) A plain A–Z list with search only.
- c) A step-by-step "what does it look like?" identification key.

**2. What should the species list be based on?**
- **a) A starter set of about 40 well-known Forest of Dean species that I write from general knowledge (recommended).** Each entry has the common and Latin name, habitat, season, key features, look-alikes and an edibility note. You'd review it before publishing, because I can't check it against your records.
- b) You send me your group's own species list or records, and I build the guide from that.
- c) A smaller set of about 15 common species, as a skeleton for you to expand.

**3. What feel do you want?**
- **a) Editorial (recommended).** Field-guide style with a serif headline face, a woodland-floor palette from leaf litter, bark and moss, and hairline rules. It looks like a printed naturalist's guide.
- b) Soft and friendly: rounded shapes, larger text and a lighter palette, aimed at families and beginners.
- c) Swiss minimal: very plain, one sans-serif face and one accent colour.

**4. What should I do about images?**
- **a) Leave a labelled photo slot on each entry and use a drawn silhouette until you have photos (recommended).** I can't source reliable, licensed mushroom photos, and a wrong photo in an ID guide is worse than none.
- b) Text only, with no image slots.
- c) You already have photos, and I'll wire them in from an `images/` folder.

I'll add one safety rule whatever you choose. The guide will say clearly that it isn't a tool for deciding what is safe to eat, and that members shouldn't eat anything on the strength of a website. Edibility will appear as a note, with the deadly species flagged prominently.

Reply with something like "1a 2a 3a 4a", or say "your call" and I'll go with the recommended options and list them as assumptions.
qa.answer:
1a, 3a and 4a. For question 2, I'd go with something close to 2c, but not exactly.

I have 16 species to start with, and each dangerous lookalike is its own entry. Please build from those 16 rather than writing a list of 40 from general knowledge. We'll add more later.

Each species should show its months, habitat, spore print colour and a few lines on telling it apart. Please don't use the word "edible" anywhere. Use only our four labels: "Eaten by members", "Not worth eating", "Poisonous" and "Deadly".

qa.asked:
I can't start the build yet, because the list of 16 species didn't come through. The `dean-fungi` folder is still empty and your message only describes the list. I'd rather wait than fill the gaps myself. A guess about a species, or about which lookalike pairs with which, is the kind of mistake that matters in an ID guide.

Please send the 16 in whatever form is easiest: pasted text, a spreadsheet export, or a file dropped into this folder. For each species I need:

- **Names:** the common name and the Latin name.
- **Months:** when the group finds it.
- **Habitat:** for example, oak woodland, conifer plantation or grassy rides.
- **Spore print colour.**
- **How to tell it apart:** a few lines in your own words. If you'd like me to draft these, say so and I'll mark them clearly for you to check.
- **Label:** one of your four, "Eaten by members", "Not worth eating", "Poisonous" or "Deadly".
- **Lookalikes:** which dangerous entry each one gets confused with, so I can link the two entries to each other.

This is how I'll build it:

- **Content:** it will use only your 16 entries and your four labels. The word "edible" won't appear anywhere on the page, including the filters and the disclaimer.
- **Lookalikes:** each dangerous lookalike will be its own entry, linked both ways to the species it's mistaken for. That way someone reading about the good species sees the warning, and someone reading the dangerous one sees what it gets mistaken for.
- **Labels:** "Poisonous" and "Deadly" will be marked with an icon and text as well as colour, so they aren't signalled by colour alone.
- **Page:** it will have search plus filters for month, habitat, spore print and label, in the Editorial style. Each entry will have a labelled photo slot with a drawn silhouette until you have photos.
- **Safety note:** the page will say that it's a reference for members and not a way of deciding what is safe to eat. I'll keep that wording free of the banned word and show it to you before it goes live.
- **Future entries:** the species will sit in one clearly marked list at the top of the file, so adding more later means adding one block.
qa.answer:
The 16 are below, with the lookalike pairs. Everything else (months, habitat, spore print, the how-to-tell-apart lines) isn't in my notes, so yes please, draft those and mark them clearly so I can check them. Labels are the same: please draft them and mark them for me to confirm. Don't guess any lookalike pairs beyond the ones here.

1. Chanterelle (*Cantharellus cibarius*). Lookalike: False chanterelle (*Hygrophoropsis aurantiaca*).
2. False chanterelle
3. Penny bun (*Boletus edulis*). Lookalike: Bitter bolete (*Tylopilus felleus*).
4. Bitter bolete
5. Giant puffball (*Calvatia gigantea*). Lookalike: Common earthball (*Scleroderma citrinum*).
6. Common earthball
7. Amethyst deceiver (*Laccaria amethystina*). Lookalike: Lilac fibrecap (*Inocybe geophylla* var. *lilacina*).
8. Lilac fibrecap
9. Hedgehog fungus (*Hydnum repandum*)
10. Beefsteak fungus (*Fistulina hepatica*)
11. Death cap (*Amanita phalloides*)
12. Destroying angel (*Amanita virosa*)
13. Deadly webcap (*Cortinarius rubellus*)
14. Fly agaric (*Amanita muscaria*)
15. Sulphur tuft (*Hypholoma fasciculare*)
16. Yellow stainer (*Agaricus xanthodermus*)

Every "Eaten by members" species must show its dangerous lookalike right beside it. Every Poisonous or Deadly entry must carry this line: "If someone may have eaten this, call 999 or NHS 111 now and keep a piece of the mushroom."

Other content for the page:
- The group has recorded 1,140 species in the Forest of Dean since 1987.
- The 2027 forays are on 5 September, 3 October and 7 November, which are the first Sundays. We meet at 10:00 at the Speech House car park.
- Our picking rule: take only what you will eat that day, and nothing from the fenced survey plots at Nagshead.
- Colours: moss green #4a5d23 on cream #f3ecd8, with red #b3261e used only for Deadly. I can send the beech woodcut.

Your plan for the safety note and the placeholder photo slots is fine. Please show me the safety wording before it goes live.
